answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with slow-thaw stake: every identity must lock a deposit before transacting, and the deposit thaws only gradually, like a glacier releasing water over months. A fake identity is cheap to mint but expensive to fund — each one ties up real capital that cannot be reused elsewhere, and misbehavior forfeits the stake. Like quartz, the deposit is hard and verifiable on chain. An ocean of ten thousand sock puppets needs ten thousand locked deposits, while one honest agent locks just one. Attack cost becomes linear in capital and time, not in free usernames.
